 JUDGMENT

This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of .1,50,000/- along with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by the petitioner.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 07.08.2021 at about 12.00 Noon, when she was travelling in Auto bearing Regn.No.KA-52-9579 along with her husband and son, on left side of road, on NH-75, Kunigal-Nelamangala Road, Opp. Bhavani Shanker House, Hanchipura Gate,
Kasaba Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, at that time the offending Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-29-BB-3922 driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly taken right side and caused accident.

Due to which, she sustained grievous injuries and thereafter she was shifted to Govt. Hospital, Nelamangala, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient and spent Rs.30,000/- towards medicine, treatment, conveyances, nourishment and attendant charges.
Prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy and she was working as a Coolie and earning a sum of Rs.18,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, she suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of lorry by its driver.
The respondents being the RC owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioner.
3. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal hence, he has been placed as ex-parte.
The respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal and filed his written statement.

4. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under:
The respondent No.2 has filed counter to petition by denying the petition averments.
He has further disputed the manner of accident, age of injured and quantum of compensation claimed under different heads.

Further contended that according to FIR, the complainant/Chikkaraju driver cum owner of autorickshaw was proceeding along with his wife and child on Bhavani Shankar House Hanchipura Gate, at that time one lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-29-BB-3922 its driver without any signal taken vehicle right side of road and the driver of autorickshaw not avoided accident and dashed to the lorry petrol tank and fell down all the persons and sustained grievous injuries.

The driver of lorry had taken all cautions with signal but the driver of Auto Smt.Nethravathi.N vs Smt.Aruna.P on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28053823/
2 without observing indication and high speedily running vehicle and selflessly dashed to lorry and sustained injuries.

Further contended that the autorickshaw cab driver cum owner was having the permit to Nelamangala Rural Area and but alleged accident occurred out of permit limit and also the owner of autorickshaw cab using the vehicle on NH-75 Road, by violating permit condition.

Further contended that the autorickshaw cab driver cum owner was holding DL to non transport and the M.V.No.KA-52-9579 Autorickshaw Cab/Passenger vehicle is transport vehicle, but he was not holding badge at the time of accident and only having 3W-NT.

Further contended that the 1st respondent is insured with this respondent under policy No.171001/31/20/P114635690 valid from 18.03.2021 to 17.03.2022 and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioner proves that, she sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 07.08.2021 at about 12.00 noon, on NH-75, Kunigal - Nelamangala Road, Opp Bhavani Shankar House, Hanchipura Gate, Kasaba Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, while she was proceeding in a Autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA-52-9579, due to the rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing registration No.TN-29-BB-3922 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?
If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3 . What order or award?
6. In order to prove her case, the petitioner examined herself as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11 and closed his side of evidence.
The respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary.
7. I have heard the arguments from both sides and perused the material available on record.

8. Findings of this tribunal on the above issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative;
 Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:-
 -:REASONS:-
Smt.Nethravathi.N vs Smt.Aruna.P on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28053823/
3
9. Issue No.1:- It is the case of petitioner that due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending lorry, the accident occurred.
The petitioner alleged that the lorry all of a sudden took towards right side, as a result the accident occurred.

The petitioner produced Ex.P2, the husband of petitioner gave statement before the police in hospital by alleging that due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle the accident occurred.
The police have registered the case as per Ex.P.1 and thereafter the police went near the place of accident and drew up mahazar as per Ex.P.4 by narrating the place of accident.
As per mahazar, the accident occurred on National Highway in between auto and lorry.
PW.1 in her chief examination deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending lorry the accident occurred.
Even in her cross examination she has deposed that due to negligence on the part of driver of lorry the accident occurred.
On meticulous perusal of evidence of PW.1, the respondent insurance company nothing elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disprove the case of petitioner.

The police after thorough investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending lorry for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 & 338 of IPC.
10.

The learned counsel for respondent insurance company vehemently argued that the Air Cab belongs to petitioners holding the permit to Nelamangala rural 5 Kms radius but the driver of Auto violated permit conditions, he was going to Tumkur District Hebbur i.e., 50 Kms, but authority issued permit only rural area 5 Kms radious and Auto was running on National Highway but the Nelamangala Traffic Police have filed charge sheet only against the lorry.

11. PW.1 in her cross examination, she has deposed that Hebburu is situated to 40-42 km from Nelamangala and on the date of accident they were coming from Hebburu to Nelamangala and auto was driving her husband.
Furhter in her cross examination, she has deposed that at the time of accident her husband was driving auto at the speed of 30 kilommeter per hour.
Further she has deposed that she has observed the lorry parked from 30 feet.
Further in her cross examination, she has deposed that the lorry all of a sudden took towards the right side as a result the accident occurred.
After investigation police filed charge sheet against the driver of offending Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-29-BB-3922.
In charge sheet it is alleged that the driver of lorry without observing the vehicle negligently took his lorry towards right side as a result the accident occurred.
Further on perusal of Ex.P.5 - Sketch, the accident occurred on National Highway in the middle of road.
Even in IMV Report mentioned the damages to auto and lorry.
As per Ex.P.8 - IMV Report, the right side rear wheel mudguard and fuel tank of right side of Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-29-BB-3922 damaged.
Ex.P.8 IMV Report corroborates case of petitioner.
The I.O has not alleged that there was a negligence on the part of petitioner, it clearly alleged that due to negligence on the part of offending lorry the accident occurred.
The respondent insurance company contended that the driver of auto violated permit conditions.
As per I.O. and case of petitioner the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of driver of offending lorry.
The respondent insurance company nothing placed before the tribunal to show that only due to negligence on the part of driver of auto the accident occurred.

Only on the basis of violation of permit condition by the driver of auto the respondent cannot escape from his liability, because the accident occurred only due to negligence on the part of driver of offending lorry.
The respondent insurance company nothing placed before the tribunal to show that only due to negligence on the part of driver of auto the accident occurred.

So,
in the absence of proof of negligence of driver of auto, the respondent insurance company cannot escape from his liability.

The respondent insurance company has not placed any materials before the Smt.Nethravathi.N vs Smt.Aruna.P on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28053823/
4 tribunal to show that the insured lorry violated terms and conditions of policy.
So, under such circumstances the respondent insurance company is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

On perusal of all the police and hospital documents placed by the petitioner, it is evident that there is a road traffic accident in the said accident in which petitioner has sustained grievous injuries due to rash and negligent driving of driver of lorry the accident occurred.

Under these circumstances,
relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.9,
this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-29-BB-3922 by its driver and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
In view of held issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury,
pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance etc.
13.
The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained lacerated wound over the left elbow and other injuries all over the body and later discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment.
In order to prove the injuries caused to her, she has produced wound certificate issued by Nelamangala Taluk Hospital marked at Ex.P.3, the doctor has opined that injury is simple in nature.
In order to prove disability, the petitioner has not produced any disability certificate or not examined the doctor to show that she has permanent disability.
The petitioner has also not produced medical bills.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor to prove her disability.
So, in the absence of proper evidence, this tribunal cannot award compensation under the head of future loss of income and other heads.

By considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also the injuries sustained by the petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of .30,000/-.
14.

In MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Page No.7 at Para No.15 held as follows:
"However, the provisions of Section 149(1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to the general law enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law overrides the general law.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in the absence of any other law relating to interest on Judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Section 34 of CPC, 1908.

Thus, in the given circumstances of this case,
interest at the rate of more than 6% could not have been awarded."

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above judgment, the petitioner is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

Smt.Nethravathi.N vs Smt.Aruna.P on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28053823/
5 15.
The petitioner has filed petition against the respondents No.1 and 2.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.TN-29-BB-3922 by its driver.
The police authorities have not filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.181 of M.V.Act.
So, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
16. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for Global  compensation amount of .30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
Entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of petitioner as amount is meager one.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of her Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
The Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer over computer, corrected and pronounced by me in open court on this 16th day of February, 2023.)
(D.RAGHAVENDRA)
